text:
AcmeAI-CS: Hi — our reserved pool 'acme-prod-1' (pool-73f4) shows ~48 GPU-hours billed between 2026-01-14T00:00Z and 2026-01-14T06:00Z but our token dashboard only shows ~12M tokens. We suspect pre-warm probes / autoscaler warmups are being charged to our commit. Invoice INV-2026-01-ACME attached. Can someone triage? :face_with_raised_eyebrow:

kelly-support: Thanks — can you paste the pool id and one example request id or header you normally send? We'll escalate to infra + billing.

AcmeAI-CS: pool id: pool-73f4. Example request header we send:
```
curl -X POST 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-XXX' \
  -H 'X-Redwood-Pool: acme-prod-1' \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
Also our app logs show a bunch of 504s around 00:05 and then a spike in GPU-hours even though no traffic.

kelly-support: got it. @omar-billing @nina-infra assigning. Omar, can you hold off billing actions pending triage? Nina, can you look for allocations with alloc_reason 'prewarm' or missing pool tag?

omar-billing: INV-2026-01-ACME noted. We'll freeze automatic invoice adjustments for now. If this is a metering bug we'll issue provisional credit; need pool_id + exact UTC window. Adding billing-bot note.

billing-bot: [automated] Ticket #TKT-98735 created, billing team notified.

nina-infra: looked at metering logs for pool-73f4. I see ~46.7 GPU-hours from 2026-01-14T00:00:12Z to 2026-01-14T05:59:58Z. Most allocations have instance_tag 'alloc_reason=prewarm'. The problem: many of those allocations are recorded without pool_label due to header being stripped by internal health probe path '/_prewarm/probe' — these probes are routed through the LB and the X-Redwood-Pool header is dropped. Logs:
```
2026-01-14T00:03:01Z alloc_id=a3f2 alloc_reason=prewarm pool_label=null instance=g4dn-12x
2026-01-14T00:03:04Z alloc_id=a3f3 alloc_reason=prewarm pool_label=null instance=g4dn-12x
```
Metering attribution rule currently uses request header to tag pool. If header missing, default attribution falls to 'reserved' bucket -> charged to commit. Likely cause.

devon-platform: confirmed. We have a codepath where the internal probe uses curl without forwarding custom headers, and the gateway strips unknown headers for probes. Short-term workaround: we've added a metering rule to attribute prewarm allocations by autoscaler group name 'acme-prod-1-warmup' for that pool; this will re-tag already-ingested events and produce a billing offset. Patching LB to preserve X-Redwood-Pool for probe routes is on PR: https://git.redwood/infra/PR/4521 (ETA today).

omar-billing: tentative credit: 46.7 GPU-hours re-attributed from committed pool to 'infra-prewarm' non-billable bucket. We'll reflect as provisional credit on INV-2026-01-ACME. Final adjustment after 48-hour verification window. Will update invoice and SLA credit if warranted.

AcmeAI-CS: thanks. Can you share what I should monitor to confirm fix? Also any repro steps we can run to validate attribution?

nina-infra: to validate: 1) trigger a small burst with header preserved, 2) check metering event:
```
GET /metering/events?alloc_id=a3xx
response: { 'alloc_id':'a3xx', 'alloc_reason':'prewarm', 'pool_label':'acme-prod-1' }
```
If pool_label is present it's fixed. For now we will reprocess the window and send an updated invoice line item.

kelly-support: I've logged the customer update. @AcmeAI-CS we'll DM when credit posts. :thumbsup:

AcmeAI-CS: appreciate the fast triage — please keep us posted. We'll hold on payments until we get the updated invoice.
